title: Secrets of Cornwall's Lost Iron Age Hill Forts Revealed | Time Team - S9 E7
description:
Discover Cornwall’s hidden Iron Age secrets as Time Team investigates two mysterious hill forts on the Lizard Peninsula, unearthing finds that rewrite ancient history.

Join the Time Team as they embark on their most ambitious dig yet, exploring the impressive prehistoric enclosures of Gear and Kervalek. Over three action-packed days, the team uncovers evidence of Iron Age and even earlier activity, revealing the sites’ roles as ancient centers of trade, ritual, and community gathering. Using cutting-edge geophysics, aerial photography, and hands-on excavation, they piece together a story stretching from the Neolithic to the Romano-British period.

Watch as the archaeologists discover Iron Age pottery, a complete sunken pot over 2,000 years old, flint arrowheads, and even a rare fragment of a Neolithic axe - all just inches below the surface. The team debates whether these “hill forts” were built for defense or as powerful statements of status and community, uncovering impressive rock-cut ditches, roundhouse remains, and clues to ancient craftsmanship. Throughout, the video delves into the challenges of protecting scheduled monuments while still unlocking their secrets for future generations.

Whether you’re fascinated by Cornish history, Iron Age archaeology, or the detective work of field archaeology, this episode offers a unique glimpse into life 2,000 years ago. See how modern technology and old-fashioned digging come together to reveal how these ancient sites shaped the region - and what mysteries remain to be solved.

#Archaeology #TimeTeam #IronAge #CornwallHistory #HillForts #Geophysics #AncientBritain #PrehistoricSites

title: Unearthing Britain’s Lost Roman Villa - Secrets of Ancient Gloucestershire | Time Team - S6 E9
description:
Step inside one of Britain’s largest Roman villas ever discovered as Time Team returns to Gloucestershire, uncovering secrets hidden beneath a quiet field for 1600 years.

In this episode, the team revisits Turkdean, where previous digs revealed an immense Roman villa complex with courtyards, bathhouses, workshops, and mysterious outbuildings. But new geophysics results suggest the site is even bigger than imagined, possibly including ritual springs, shrines, and an intricate water system. Follow the archaeologists as they open new trenches, unearth painted wall plaster, mosaics, coins, brooches, and evidence of both domestic luxury and industrial activity. Watch as theories evolve - was this extra range a temple, a “granny wing,” or something entirely unexpected?

As discoveries mount, learn about Roman life in Gloucestershire: from villa estate infrastructure to ritual offerings in the springs, and the social rise of local aristocrats under Roman rule. The team reconstructs how the villa evolved over centuries, revealing a high-status residence complete with painted rooms, cellars, and even towered entrances. Special highlights include an authentic Roman altar dedication, ancient pigments in action, and the ingenious tracing of the villa’s water source. Perfect for anyone interested in Roman Britain, archaeology, or Time Team’s signature blend of history and hands-on exploration.

title: Uncovering the Secret Furnace That Sparked the Industrial Revolution | Time Team - S9 E5
description:
Step into the secret world beneath a Shropshire pub, where Time Team uncovers a hidden blast furnace that helped ignite the Industrial Revolution.

Join the Time Team as they race against the clock to reveal the secrets of Leighton's forgotten furnace, buried under a village pub just miles from Ironbridge - the cradle of the Industrial Revolution. Discover how this 17th-century blast furnace operated, from its roaring charcoal fires and massive waterwheel-powered bellows to the casting of cannonballs for the English Civil War. Watch as the team reconstructs the ancient process of making charcoal, traces the ingenious water management systems in the surrounding landscape, and unearths evidence of the bustling ironworks that once shaped the local community.

This episode delves into the fascinating transition from traditional charcoal-fueled ironmaking to Abraham Darby's revolutionary use of coke at nearby Ironbridge. See firsthand how archaeological detective work, historical documents, and hands-on experiments piece together the story of how Leighton's furnace fit into the wider industrial landscape. Whether you're passionate about industrial archaeology, British history, or the roots of modern technology, this dig brings history to life beneath your feet.

title: Unearthing Rycote Park - Lost Tudor Palace and Its Royal Secrets Revealed | Time Team - S8 E6
description:
Discover the secrets of Rycote Park's lost Tudor palace, once host to five monarchs, as Time Team races to uncover its hidden remains in just three days.

Join the Time Team as they delve into the fascinating history and archaeology of Rycote Park in Oxfordshire. Once a grand Tudor mansion welcoming the likes of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I, Rycote mysteriously vanished after a devastating 18th-century fire. With only a few ruins, old engravings, and scattered masonry to guide them, the team faces the challenge of pinpointing the house’s true footprint, the location of its moat, and the fate of its opulent halls. Watch as experts compare historical prints, employ geophysics, and dig trenches to piece together the evolution of this royal residence, uncovering clues from Tudor brickwork to medieval walls buried beneath Capability Brown’s landscaped gardens.

Throughout the dig, you'll witness the discovery of the great hall’s dazzling floor tiles, fragments of stained glass, and evidence of lavish Tudor banquets, all while unraveling the truth behind the estate's fiery destruction and surprising post-fire rebuilding. The investigation reveals not just the palace's rise and fall, but also its earlier medieval roots and the ultimate asset-stripping that led to its disappearance. Perfect for history buffs, archaeology fans, and anyone curious about how England’s grandest homes could simply vanish.

#Archaeology #TimeTeam #TudorHistory #RycotePark #LostPalace #ElizabethanEngland #HistoricalMystery #BritishHistory

title: Unearthing the Lost Viaduct - Secrets of the World's First Railway Bridge | Time Team - S8 E5
description:
Step into the hunt for the world's first railway viaduct, lost beneath the industrial landscape of South Wales. Will Time Team uncover the hidden arches of Blaina Niven?

Join Time Team as they journey to Blaenavon in South Wales, seeking the elusive 18th-century railway viaduct that once revolutionized coal transport during the Industrial Revolution. Using ground-penetrating radar, historical maps, and massive excavations, the team faces the challenge of a landscape transformed by centuries of mining spoil and industrial waste. As they search for both the lost viaduct and the workers’ cottages buried beneath layers of debris, discover how the region's history was shaped by ironmasters, miners, and families whose lives vanished beneath the surface.

This episode showcases industrial archaeology at its most dramatic, with giant diggers shifting thousands of tons of earth, archaeologists piecing together clues from pottery shards and iron rails, and a fascinating look at the lives of workers who lived beneath viaduct arches. Witness the recreation of historic iron casting and the emotional moment when the team finally glimpses the buried viaduct’s arches for the first time in 200 years. Whether you’re passionate about railway history, the Industrial Revolution, or the thrill of a great archaeological mystery, this adventure brings the lost world of Blaenavon vividly to life.

title: The Mystery of the Fake Ancient Welsh Spring - Archaeological Investigation | Time Team - S8 E3
description:
Step into a mysterious Welsh valley where Time Team uncovers an archaeological puzzle: ancient artefacts, a "holy spring," and a sword buried in modern mud. Is this history or hoax?

Join the Time Team as they investigate a site in Wales filled with standing stones, a supposed Neolithic tomb, early Christian carvings, and a spring yielding Roman coins and jewelry. The team dives into the mystery of why so many artefacts from different eras have surfaced in one place, questioning whether this is an untouched holy site or an elaborate Victorian invention. Watch as experts analyze coins, brooches, and even a rare Iron Age La Tène sword, only to discover it was lying on top of modern barbed wire, casting doubt on its origins.

Throughout their three-day forensic dig, the archaeologists unravel the truth behind the site's features - from the "Neolithic tomb" built just decades ago, to the "Norman tower" and animal shed with early Christian symbols. They reveal how a 19th-century cleric, Thomas Price, and possibly others, may have created or enhanced the site's antiquarian allure. Discover how the lack of archaeological context for these finds, including coins and ritual objects, points to recent "salting" of the site rather than genuine ancient activity.

This episode highlights the crucial importance of context in archaeology, showing how misplaced artefacts can obscure real history. Dive in to find out how the Time Team solved the riddle of this Welsh "historical theme park" and why context is everything in uncovering the past.

#Archaeology #TimeTeam #AncientMysteries #WelshHistory #ArchaeologicalHoax #RomanArtefacts #IronAgeSword #HistoricalInvestigation

title: Unearthing Coventry’s Lost Medieval Cathedral - Secrets Beneath the City | Time Team - S7 E7
description:
Step inside the lost world of medieval Coventry as Time Team uncovers the secrets of St Mary’s - the city’s forgotten first cathedral. What lies beneath Priory Row?

Join Time Team’s three-day archaeological dig as they search for Coventry’s original cathedral, St Mary’s, destroyed by Henry VIII and hidden beneath modern streets. This episode reveals how geophysics, excavation, and expert research come together to reconstruct the mighty Norman-Gothic structure that once symbolized Coventry’s power. From uncovering ancient walls, painted glass, and medieval tiles to investigating mysterious burials and even potential crime scenes, the team faces unpredictable weather, urban obstacles, and historical puzzles at every turn.

Watch as the archaeologists locate the central crossing piers, reveal the chapter house, and piece together the daily lives of Benedictine monks. Experience the drama of discovering a probable prior’s grave, the challenge of reconstructing stained glass using medieval methods, and the thrill of building a detailed 3D model of St Mary’s Cathedral for the first time in centuries. If you’re fascinated by British history, lost architecture, or the excitement of real-time discovery, this episode is a must-watch!

title: Unearthing Wadden: 4000 Years of Secrets Beneath a Dorset Village | Time Team - S7 E4
description:
Discover how a Dorset garden revealed secrets of Iron Age roundhouses, medieval life, and a mysterious 4000-year-old henge - all in just three days of archaeology!

Join Time Team as they investigate the tiny village of Wadden in Dorset, where residents David and Grace stumbled upon ancient pottery in their back gardens. What starts as curiosity about lumps and bumps in the fields quickly unravels into a thrilling archaeological adventure. Using geophysics, expert excavation, and experimental pottery-making, the team uncovers evidence of early Iron Age settlements, a medieval cottage, and, most astonishingly, a Neolithic henge monument possibly dating back to 2500 BC.

In this episode, you'll see how layers of history overlap: from fresh Iron Age pottery sherds and reconstructed roundhouse walls to medieval kilns and cider cisterns. Watch as the team reconstructs ancient pottery techniques, explores centuries-old field systems, and pieces together Wadden's story through finds, landscape clues, and historical records. Alongside the excitement of new discoveries, enjoy the human stories of David and Grace as their garden transforms into a portal to Britain's distant past. Perfect for fans of archaeology, British history, and those fascinated by how ordinary places can hide extraordinary secrets beneath the surface.

description:
Uncover the lost story of a WWII Spitfire and its young pilot, Paul Klipsch, as Time Team excavates a forgotten crash site in northern France.

Join the Time Team as they embark on a gripping three-day mission to locate and recover one of the earliest Mark I Spitfires lost during the Battle of France. Through expert archaeology, eyewitness accounts, and the help of aviation historians, the team pieces together the fate of pilot Paul Klipsch, who was killed in action on his very first day of combat. This episode is a unique blend of wartime history, crash investigation, and hands-on restoration. You'll witness meticulous fieldwork, hear from those who knew Klipsch, and see original Spitfire parts restored using period techniques. Discover how the team interprets clues from machine guns, bullet impacts, and cockpit remains to unravel the tragic final moments of a young RAF pilot. title: Uncovering Medieval Islamic Spain - Secrets of Denia's Lost City Revealed | Time Team - S7 E1
description:
Discover the lost Islamic city beneath modern Denia, Spain, as Time Team uncovers 900 years of hidden history and reveals how this port shaped Europe’s medieval world.

Join the Time Team as they dig deep into Denia on Spain’s Costa Blanca, unearthing the remarkable story of an Islamic town that once rivaled the great cities of Cairo and Baghdad. Through rescue archaeology, the team explores the remains of Al-Andalus: walled suburbs, ancient cemeteries, bustling markets, and advanced pottery kilns, all hidden under today’s streets. Learn how Arab, Berber, and African settlers transformed this Mediterranean port from the 8th to 13th centuries, bringing groundbreaking innovations in science, mathematics, and cuisine to Europe. The excavation reveals how Denia’s Islamic heritage influenced everything from burial practices (Muslims buried facing Mecca, with no grave goods or headstones) to the introduction of citrus fruits, spices, and sophisticated ceramics—pottery technology centuries ahead of its time in Britain.

Watch as the team investigates skeletons for clues about medieval diets and diseases, reconstructs lost city walls and bridges, and even cooks up authentic 10th-century Islamic recipes like lamb with prunes and date pie. The discoveries paint a vivid picture of a multicultural trading hub, where people from North Africa, the Middle East, and Europe lived side by side. From medieval shops and bustling harbors to the everyday lives of craftspeople and merchants, this episode uncovers the vibrant legacy of Islamic Spain, just below the surface of a popular holiday destination.

title: Lost Jamestown Found: Unearthing Nevis's Hidden History | Time Team - S6 E13
description:
Uncover the lost secrets of Nevis: from the vanished capital of Jamestown to the island's first-ever discovered slave village and ancient Amerindian settlements.

Join us for a captivating archaeological adventure across Nevis as we search for the long-lost Jamestown, investigate the island's earliest Amerindian inhabitants, and reveal the daily lives of African slaves hidden in the island’s overgrown terrain. Our journey is packed with discoveries - from centuries-old pottery and mysterious artifacts to forgotten fortresses and myths of tidal waves that changed local history.

In this episode, our team uses cutting-edge geophysics, historical records, and hands-on excavation to piece together Nevis’s past. We’ll walk through rain-soaked jungles, sift through coastal sands, and decode centuries-old maps to challenge local legends. See how we identify rare Amerindian postholes, reconstruct prehistoric huts, and unearth evidence that rewrites the story of Jamestown’s fate after the 1680 earthquake. Along the way, we reveal the contrasts between the grand lifestyles of English plantation owners and the resilience of the enslaved Africans who shaped Nevisian society. You’ll also learn about the plants, tools, and daily life of the island’s earliest residents, and how their legacy still echoes today.

Whether you’re fascinated by Caribbean history, archaeology, or the untold stories of lost communities, this deep dive into Nevis’s hidden past will surprise and inspire you. Watch as lost stories come alive through artifacts, landscapes, and local legends - and discover how archaeology can transform our understanding of the past.

title: Uncovering the Lost Slave Village of Nevis - Caribbean Archaeology Revealed | Time Team - S6 E12
description:

Join the Time Team on the Caribbean island of Nevis, where centuries-old ruins and dense jungle conceal the remains of once-lavish sugar estates and the untold stories of those who lived and labored there. In this episode, the team investigates the Mount Travers plantation, once owned by the wealthy Pinney family, whose fortunes were built on sugar and slave labor. As modern development threatens to erase this history forever, the archaeologists race against time to map the estate, excavate its grand house, and search for evidence of the slave village and early sugar production sites.

You’ll see how the team uses historic documents, maps, and first-hand accounts to reconstruct plantation life, from the luxury enjoyed by owners to the harsh conditions faced by enslaved Africans. Watch as they dig through layers of pottery, glass, and architecture to date the site, reveal a possible slave jail or hurricane shelter, and experiment with traditional sugar-making. Along the way, local experts and descendants help piece together Nevis’s unique past, while the search for the lost slave village pushes the team deep into the overgrown landscape. This video offers a rare glimpse into the complex history of the Caribbean’s sugar islands, the wealth and suffering they produced, and the ongoing efforts to preserve their archaeological heritage.

title: Unearthing a Lost Roman Bathhouse and Ironworks in British Woods | Time Team - S6 E7
description:
Discover how a Roman bathhouse was found on a Sussex golf course, revealing secrets of ancient ironworking and a mysterious lost settlement! Roman iron smelting in Britain comes alive.

Join the Time Team as they investigate the astonishing discovery of a Roman bathhouse hidden between the fairways of Beauport Park Golf Course near Hastings. Unearthed by amateur archaeologist Gerald Broderib, this remarkably preserved site features underfloor heating, tiled walls, and windows - but it’s isolated, standing alone 40 miles from the nearest Roman town. Why was such an impressive structure built here, and what was happening in these woods nearly 2,000 years ago?

The team uncovers evidence linking the bathhouse to a vast Roman ironworking operation, complete with heaps of slag and tiles stamped with the Classis Britannica - the Roman navy’s mark. Over three days, they use archaeological digs, geophysics, and experimental iron smelting to piece together the story of this industrial hub. Did a thriving Roman settlement exist here, or was the bathhouse just a comfort for overseers amid a sea of laborers? Explore the challenges of woodland archaeology, the debate over high-status Roman buildings, and the excitement of recreating ancient iron production.

If you’re fascinated by Roman Britain, lost settlements, or the secrets beneath your feet, this episode uncovers how industrial might shaped the landscape - and the lives - of ancient Sussex.

#Archaeology #RomanBritain #TimeTeam #IronSmelting #BeauportPark #LostSettlements #AncientHistory #SussexHistory

title: Uncovering a 3,000-Year-Old Bronze Age Mystery in the Somerset Levels | Time Team - S5 E2
description:
Unearthing a Bronze Age mystery: join us as we search for ancient trackways beneath the Somerset Levels and build our own prehistoric timber path in just three days!

What lies hidden under the Somerset peat? In this immersive archaeological adventure, we set out to locate a lost timber trackway—possibly over 3,000 years old—using clues from a 1926 excavation, geophysical surveys, and hands-on detective work. As we dig through layers of history, uncovering ancient planks, Iron Age pottery, and even human bones, the site reveals itself to be far more complex than a simple wooden road. Could this be a ritual boundary, a burial platform, or something else entirely?

Alongside the excavation, we challenge ourselves to reconstruct a prehistoric trackway using authentic Bronze Age and Iron Age tools. Watch as we split oak with hand-forged axes, learn traditional woodworking techniques, and discover firsthand the ingenuity needed to cross the ancient marshlands. With expert insights into dendrochronology, pollen analysis, and environmental clues, we piece together the landscape and life of prehistoric Somerset. The journey uncovers not just a structure, but a mystery that rewrites what we know about Britain's ancient past.

#Archaeology #BronzeAge #SomersetLevels #PrehistoricBritain #AncientTrackway #ExperimentalArchaeology #Dendrochronology #IronAgeHistory

title: Unearthing Malton: Secrets of the Medieval Castle and Jacobean Mansion | Time Team - S4 E5
description:
Step into 2,000 years of hidden English history as we uncover Malton’s lost medieval castle, Jacobean mansion, and Roman fort beneath an overgrown jungle.

Join us in North Yorkshire as a determined team of archaeologists races against time - and a jungle of nettles - to reveal the secrets beneath Malton’s green heart. In just three days, we search for the legendary medieval castle, trace the outlines of a Jacobean mansion, and unearth remnants of a Roman fort, all while balancing modern development plans and the strict rules protecting this ancient site. You’ll see real archaeological strategy in action, the challenges of working with limited trenches, and the excitement of every new discovery, from medieval pottery and castle walls to clues of grand gardens and dramatic sieges.

Along the way, meet passionate local residents and learn how the findings could inspire a new community park, connecting the rich layers of Malton’s past to its future. Watch as history comes alive: swords are forged, knights’ armor is donned, and centuries-old mysteries are pieced together through hands-on digging, aerial surveys, and expert analysis. Will the team find both the castle and the mansion? And what does it all reveal about the turbulent history of this remarkable town?

#Archaeology #Malton #MedievalCastle #RomanFort #JacobeanMansion #TimeTeam #BritishHistory #YorkshireHistory

title: Searching for King Connor's Lost Palaces - Ancient Ulster Unearthed | Time Team - S3 E5
description:
Step into the real legends of Ulster as Time Team investigates ancient palaces, mysterious ditches, and early Christian secrets in the landscape of Navan, Northern Ireland.

Join the team as they explore Owen Macha, searching for King Connor's legendary third palace mentioned in the epic Irish tales of the Táin. Across three action-packed days, archaeologists dig into the myth and history of sites like Creve Row, Haughey's Fort, and Ballydoo, guided by ancient stories and cutting-edge geophysics. Along the way, they uncover Neolithic axes, Bronze Age pottery, medieval artifacts, and even rare early Christian finds, revealing how generations shaped this sacred landscape.

You'll witness the excitement of new discoveries, from prehistoric rock art to the remains of massive ditches that may have once marked out royal or ritual boundaries. The team also recreates Iron Age bronze-working, bringing to life the craftsmanship and prestige of Ulster's ancient elite. Whether it's debating the true origins of place names, connecting archaeological evidence to heroic legends, or unraveling mysteries buried beneath centuries of history, this episode brings you right to the heart of Ireland's past.

If you’re fascinated by Irish mythology, ancient settlements, or the detective work of archaeology, this is a journey you won’t want to miss!

title: Mystery of the 16th Century Shipwreck - Time Team's Underwater Discovery | Time Team - S3 E4
description:
Dive into the thrilling hunt for a mysterious 16th-century shipwreck off the Devon coast - can underwater archaeology finally reveal its secrets?

Join the Time Team as they tackle their first ever underwater excavation, searching for clues to identify a centuries-old shipwreck found near Tinmouth. Using cutting-edge geophysical surveys, magnetometers, and hands-on diving, the team investigates the ship's remains buried beneath layers of sand, unearthing cannons, merchant seals, and timber. Could this wreck be a lost vessel from the Spanish Armada, or was it a Venetian merchant ship caught in a deadly storm? Discover how experts reconstruct the ship’s story by examining artifacts, analyzing heraldry on ancient cannons, and exploring Tinmouth’s historic port buildings.

You’ll witness the challenges of underwater trench digging, learn how 16th-century cannons were loaded and fired, and see how stormy seas and shifting sands complicate the search for answers. Watch as the team uncovers preserved ship timbers and "ghost nails," piece together evidence from local museums, and reconstruct the final voyage of this enigmatic vessel. If you’re fascinated by maritime mysteries, shipwreck archaeology, or British history, this episode is packed with discoveries, expert insights, and suspenseful twists right up to the final dive.

#Archaeology #Shipwreck #TimeTeam #UnderwaterArchaeology #SpanishArmada #MaritimeHistory #DevonCoast #HistoricalDiscovery

title: Secrets of the Knights Templar Unearthed at Templecombe | Time Team - S3 E3
description:
Step inside Templecombe, Somerset, as Time Team hunts for the lost remains of the Knights Templar and uncovers secrets hidden for centuries beneath this historic village.

Join the team as they unravel the true story of the legendary Templars in England, from investigating mysterious medieval floor tiles and a 13th-century chapel to deciphering ancient maps and boundary walls. Discover how a seemingly ordinary manor house and farm fields might hold the keys to the past, as archaeologists dig through layers of history to reveal the life, rituals, and daily workings of the fighting monks who once called Templecombe home. Along the way, you'll learn how the Templars financed their operations, why their structures were so elusive, and how their presence shaped local history. The episode blends archaeological detective work with tales of brewing medieval ale, examining Templar rulebooks, and sorting fact from legend about these enigmatic knights.

Watch as discoveries unfold - from encaustic tiles marked with noble coats of arms to the elusive monastic boundary wall that had been hiding in plain sight. See how historic buildings are dated with dendrochronology, how expert survey work redefines centuries-old assumptions, and how the team overcomes setbacks to finally piece together the Templar preceptory’s layout. Whether you're fascinated by the Crusades, medieval architecture, or the mysteries of the Knights Templar, this episode brings their story vividly to life through hands-on exploration and historical insight.

#Archaeology #TimeTeam #KnightsTemplar #Templecombe #MedievalHistory #HistoricEngland #CrusaderMysteries #AncientBuildings

title: Did We Just Find the Real First Roman Road in London? | Time Team - S2 E4
description:
Discover the mystery of London’s first Roman road and the true birthplace of the city - could centuries of history be rewritten by new archaeological evidence?

Join the investigation as we retrace the steps of Roman legions, question long-held beliefs, and use cutting-edge technology to search for the lost Roman road beneath London. Archaeologists revisit a 60-year-old discovery, dig trenches at Lambeth Palace, analyze Roman pottery, and reconstruct the ancient landscape with 3D mapping and geophysical surveys. Learn why the Romans chose their river crossing points, how geography shaped the rise of Londinium, and what clues remain buried under modern London.

From exploring marshy banks and sandbars in the Thames to uncovering the significance of Stanegate and Thorny Island, this episode dives deep into the origins of London’s road network and settlement patterns. Will the team confirm the original crossing point, or will new findings challenge everything we thought we knew about Roman London? Perfect for history buffs, archaeology fans, and anyone fascinated by the hidden stories beneath our cities.

description:

title: Norman Neighbours (Full Episode) | S12 EP11 | Time Team (Skipsea, Yorkshire)
description:
For years Time Team fan Frances Davies has been collecting finds from the field outside her back door in Skipsea in East Yorkshire. She has uncovered Neolithic, Roman and Saxon items, but her best finds are medieval pots dating from the Norman Conquest. It's clear that there was some habitation in the area 1,000 years ago, but a geophysics plot of the site reveals incredible results, far beyond the team's expectations. Could Frances have had a whole Norman village in her field, a village lost to the records? And could there be a clue in nearby Skipsea Castle, the seat of power of the Norman overlord of the whole area? The Team have three days to find out.

title: The Puzzle of Picket's Farm (Full Episode) | S12 EP10 | Time Team (South Perrott, Dorset)
description:
Time Team heads to South Perrott in Dorset, inspired by the intriguing discovery of Roman brooches and coins in a hilltop field. The Team are pretty sure they're going to uncover a Roman Temple, but the search gets off to a bad start when all the pottery turns out to be medieval and there's no sign of any buildings. Something has clearly been going on in this field, but it's not what they thought. The trenches gradually reveal their contents, painting a very different picture from a very different
period. Have the Team stumbled across a Stone Age burial site that had, extraordinarily, been honoured for thousands of years right into Roman times? Prehistory specialist Miles Russell explains some aspects of Bronze Age features.

description:

title: Blood, Sweat and Beers (Full Episode) | S16 EP5 | Time Team (Rise Hill, Cumbria)
description:
Tony Robinson ventures to the wild and windswept heights of the Yorkshire Dales to uncover a story of murder, suicide and heroic endurance against the elements. In an archaeological first, the team investigate a settlement lived in by the railway navvies, itinerant construction workers who moved from site to site looking for work. While much is known about their construction techniques, virtually nothing is known about the life they led in these remote locations.

The Team face digging through a church graveyard in search of what could be one of the largest Roman structures ever built in Britain. Groby Old Hall in Leicestershire was once home to the legendary White Queen: Elizabeth, the wife of Edward IV. description:

So, she called in Tony Robinson and the team to help her unravel the mystery of their mill.

description:

title: The Domesday Mill (Full Episode) | S14 EP9 | Time Team (Dotton, Devon)
description:
After you watch this episode, check out the official commentary video on the Time Team Official YouTube Channel! https://youtu.be/QiZ4Si_cZIA

Tony and the team travel to the banks of the River Otter in Devon to dig a `Time Team' first: a watermill. It's a small site but the challenge facing the team is huge: they have over 900 years of history to investigate. `The Domesday Book' of 1086 records a mill at Dotton, while the last mill on this site was pulled down as recently as the 1960s. It's down to the diggers to work out what happened here between those dates.

description:
After you watch this episode, check out the official commentary video on the Time Team Official YouTube Channel! https://youtu.be/yS573eYxu4k

Wemyss Caves, on the shore of the Firth of Forth, have been a famous landmark for centuries. Legend has it that they were occupied by Pictish people who scared the Romans into building Hadrian's Wall and that later they were home to medieval Christian hermits and later to Jacobean nobles. Now the caves are under serious threat from erosion from the sea, but the caves have never been properly investigated.

description:
After you watch this episode, check out the official commentary video on the Time Team Official YouTube Channel!  https://youtu.be/xSOmEhmeJ7o

Street of the Dead Tony and the team tackle a huge Roman fort in County Durham. The stronghold was part of the defence of Dere Street, the main Roman road from York to Hadrian's Wall. The fort has fine mosaics and preserved rooms, but the Team have just three days to find out everything they can about the 'vicus', that's the civilian settlement around the fort, vital for the smooth running of the military machine and providing for the pleasures of the men garrisoned there. However, they soon discover something even more exciting during the dig - a series of military mausoleums, the first discovery of its kind for over 150 years.

title: Mystery of the Ice Cream Villa (Full Episode) | S16 EP8 | Time Team (Yelnow Villa, Colworth)
description:
Stacks of high quality Roman remains have been found in a rural field near an ice cream research centre, including a huge collection of coins. It points to a high status building, possibly a villa. But it's far from any road, and geophysics doesn't come up with anything definite, apart from a large square ditch. Stewart identifies a potential Roman road, running right past the site. Though they are unable to find a substantial stone building, the outline of an Iron Age round house emerges, showing continuity of occupation over hundreds or thousands of years. Late on day three, evidence of a Roman structure emerges. They are joined by Roman coin specialist Philippa Walton, Ben Robinson from Peterborough City Council and Louise Revell from Southampton University.

description:

In South Shields, the Roman Fort at the end of Hadrian's Wall is a local landmark and the team embark on a quest to locate the site of a huge Roman military cemetery thought to be in the area. They search all nearby open spaces but come to the conclusion that the likeliest site of the cemetery is beneath a 1960s housing estate. A few tombstones and burials have been found in the past hundred years, but there must be a huge Roman military cemetery somewhere. Time Team use every spare piece of open space, have a look under the occasional pavement and enlist as much local help, young and old, as possible in their hunt for the site. It's three days of head-scratching mayhem before the answer emerges.

description:

For years Time Team fan Frances Davies has been collecting finds from the field outside her back door in Skipsea in East Yorkshire. She has uncovered Neolithic, Roman and Saxon items, but her best finds are medieval pots dating from the Norman Conquest. title: Lost Centuries at St Osyth (Full Episode) | S12 EP9 | Time Team (Essex)
description:
After you watch this episode, check out the official commentary video on the Time Team Official YouTube Channel! : https://youtu.be/ESyt5zkSvUw

Century Viking pirates sailed up a muddy Essex creek. Legend has it they captured a lonely nun who when offered her modesty or her mortality, chose to die. The nun then carried her severed head up the hill to her church where she collapsed. Where she lay a spring bubbled up. The nun was St Osyth, the wife of the Saxon King of Essex, who chose the veil rather than consummating her marriage. The site of her death became a shrine and a busy settlement grew up. In the 12th Century Richard de Belmais, Bishop of London, founded a large Augustinian Priory in the middle of the village. This became a powerful establishment, which by the Dissolution in 1539 was one of the wealthiest Augustinian Monasteries in Europe. A few years ago a local boatbuilder noticed some decayed timbers sticking out of the mud in St Osyth Creek. The tides gradually revealed more of these timbers, which are on a significant bend in the channel. These timbers could be the remains of a medieval wharf which served the town in its early days, but they could also be the key to a much bigger mystery.
The present town seems to date to the 15th century but the famous Priory is much older. There must have been a busy settlement servicing it - so where was the original town of St Osyth? Time Team have three days to redraw the map of this picturesque town on the Essex coast.
